note.note:
Consult Summary:
- Patient with known asthma reporting 2–3 days of wheeze, cough, and exertional shortness of breath; probable small asthma exacerbation. Advised interim inhaler adjustments and urgent face-to-face GP review.

History:
- Presenting complaint:
  - 2–3 days of progressive shortness of breath, worse with running and brisk walking.
  - Associated wheeze and cough.
  - No sputum production.
  - Blue (salbutamol) inhaler reported as not adequately relieving symptoms.
- Symptom course:
  - Symptoms began 2–3 days ago and worsened recently; asthma previously well controlled until this episode.
  - Last significant asthma attack ~3–4 years ago.
  - Last asthma review ~2 years ago.
- Past medical history / allergies / medications:
  - Asthma (longstanding; intermittent exacerbations).
  - Hay fever reported.
  - Possible eczema (patient uncertain; family history of eczema noted).
  - No known drug allergies (patient stated none).
  - Medications reported:
    - Salbutamol (blue inhaler) — dose/route/frequency not documented; patient reports using as needed and also reported using morning/evening at one point (conflict noted).
    - Brown inhaler “Clenil” (preventer) — reported use twice daily (dose not documented).
    - Topical agents: patient initially listed "Flanel Bactroban and Hydrocortisone" then corrected to "Cetraben and Hydrocortisone" (conflict noted; dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Social history / preventive care:
  - No smoking status, occupation, or vaccination status documented.

Examination:
- Vitals: not documented.
- Physical exam findings: none documented (no chest exam performed during this consult).

Impression:
- Probable mild asthma exacerbation.

Plan:
- Interim self-management (while awaiting GP review):
  - Use salbutamol (blue inhaler) as needed, maximum every 2–4 hours; if using this frequently, indicates poor control and need for urgent review.
  - Increase brown inhaler (Clenil) to four puffs twice daily while awaiting review (advice given by clinician).
- Arrange face-to-face GP assessment within the next few days for:
  - Chest examination and formal peak flow measurement.
  - Consideration of oral steroids and/or antibiotics depending on findings.
- Safety advice:
  - If breathing markedly worsens before the appointment, go to Accident & Emergency immediately rather than waiting.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Current vital signs (respiratory rate, heart rate, oxygen saturation, temperature, blood pressure).
  - Current objective peak flow while symptomatic.
  - Exact inhaler types, strengths, and doses (salbutamol dose; Clenil dose per puff).
  - Exact route/dose/frequency for topical medications (Cetraben, hydrocortisone) and confirmation of Bactroban status.
  - Smoking status, pregnancy status (if applicable), and vaccination (influenza, pneumococcal) status.
  - Current list of all medications (reconciliation) and adherence details.
- Internal conflicts from transcript:
  - Medication names: patient initially stated "Flanel Bactroban and Hydrocortisone" then corrected to "Cetraben and Hydrocortisone" (conflict noted).
  - Preventer inhaler color/type: patient initially implied the preventer is "blue"; clinician described the preventer as brown (Clenil) (conflict noted).
  - Frequency of salbutamol use: patient described both "as and when" and "every day morning or evening" (conflict noted).
- Transcript quality:
  - Generally understandable but several words/names were unclear or partially inaudible, contributing to medication/name confusion.
